key_insight: SQUARE replaces a frozen LM adapter with a compact quantum-inspired feature map that turns a bottleneck vector into normalized quadratic interactions via amplitude encoding, a parameterized circuit, and measurement.
engineering_relevance: It offers a structured way to model pairwise feature interactions with shared parameters in a small adapter, which is useful for reranking, scoring, and preference modeling on top of frozen language models.
method: Amplitude-encode the bottleneck vector into a quantum state.
Apply a parameterized quantum circuit and measure basis probabilities plus Pauli-Z readouts.
Use the measured outputs as a compact structured quadratic feature map over O(d^2) coordinate pairs.
evidence_signal: Across eight GLUE-derived controlled interaction tasks and five seeds, SQUARE averaged 0.7565 test accuracy, outperforming the affine normalized-quadratic predictor (0.7355), Givens mixing (0.7271), MLP (0.6817), and frozen-circuit control (0.6155).
watch_item: Results are based on circuit simulation rather than hardware, so efficiency, noise tolerance, and runtime on real quantum devices remain unverified.
paper_title: SQUARE: Structured Quantum Representation Adapters as Compact Quadratic Feature Maps for Frozen Language Models
